facts: Workspace identity is the directory of the NEAREST ANCESTOR pom.xml of the path in the tool call — not a caller-supplied session, and not 'the last workspace used'. Routing is re-derived from the call's own argument every time (INV-ROUTE-1).

A multi-module Maven build gets exactly ONE workspace, at the OUTERMOST pom.xml that declares <modules> (the reactor root) — not one workspace per module. JDT LS's own multi-root support is a known-weak path (upstream issue 1303: 'only one of them will work').

A path with no ancestor pom.xml must return an explicit error naming the path, never an empty successful result (INV-ROUTE-2) — this matters because JDT LS itself answers a misrouted query with [], an empty array, not an error (spike B), so this component is the only place that can prevent that ambiguity from reaching the caller.

X-005 (open cross-cutting decision, docs/cross-cutting.md): the recommended workspace-identity key is the absolute REALPATH of the reactor-root directory, hashed for the -data path, with symlinks resolved before hashing so two paths to one project are one workspace. This is a recommendation, not yet a closed decision — implement it, but do not treat the specific hash algorithm as settled beyond 'stable and collision-free for this feature's own tests'.

A-006 (docs/assumptions.md) — 'nearest ancestor pom.xml, one workspace per reactor root' — is status 'assumed', not 'verified' or 'needs-human'. It does not block implementation; it is listed so the blast radius is visible if a later spike contradicts it.
